3. Interpretation-clause.----In
this Act, unless there be something repugnant in the sub ject or context,-
"land" includes the
sites of villages, towns and cities: it also includes trees; growing crops and
grass, fruit .upon, and juice in trees, rights-of-way, ferries, fisheries and
all other benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth or
permanently fastened to things attached to the earth:
"land-revenue" means
all sums and payments, in money or in kind, received or claimable by or on
behalf (Subs. by the A. O., 1937, for "of
Government" and then amended by P.O. 1 of 1964, Art. 2, w.e.f. 23rd March,
1956, to read as above.)[of the Government] from any person on account
of any land held by or vested in him, and any cess or rate authorized (Subs. ibid, for "by Government".)[by the
Provincial Government] under the provisions of any law for the time being in
force
"Revenue-officer" means
any officer employed in or about the business of the land-revenue, or of the
surveys, assessment, accounts or records connected therewith.

[28th March, 1876]
7. Punishment or prosecution of Revenue-officer no bar to civil
remedies.-----Nothing in any law for the time being in force which autho rizes
the punishment departmentally of any Revenue-officer for any offence or breach
of duty, or which sanctions his prosecution crimi nally for such offence or
breach, shall be held to bar any remedy which may be had in the Civil Court
against such officer.

11. Suits not to be
entertained unless plaintiff has exhausted right of appeal.----No. Civil
Court shall entertain any suit (Subs. by the A. O.,
1937, for "against Government" and finally the word" Govern ment"
was subs. for the word "crown" by P. O. No. 1 of 1961.)[against
the Government) on account of any act or omission of any Revenue officer
unless the plaintiff first proves that, previously to bringing his suit, he has
presented all such appeals allowed by the law for the time being in force as,
within the period of limitation allowed for bringing such suit, it was possible
to present.

Power of Provincial Government to refer questions for decision of High Court

Act No

(For statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India,

12. Power of Provincial
Government to refer questions for decision of High Court.-----If, in the
trial or investigation of any suit, claim or objec tion which, but for the
passing of this Act, might have been tried or investigated by a Civil Court,
there arises any question on which on (The words
"the G. G. in C" rep. by the A. O., 1937.)* * * * the (Subs. ibld, for "L. G.".)[Provincial
Government] desires to have the decision of the (Subs.
by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960 , for "Chief Court".)[High
Court], (The words "the G. G. in C" rep. by
the A. O., 1937.)* * * the (Subs. ibld, for
"L. G.".)[Provincial Government] (The
words "as the case may be" rep. by the A.O. 1937.)* * * may
cause a statement of the question to be prepared, and may refer such question
for the decision of the [High Court].
The said (Subs. by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960 for "Chief Court of Sind")[High
Court] shall fix an early day for the hearing of the question referred, and
cause notice of such day to be placed in the court-house.
The parties to the case may
appear and be heard in the (Subs. by Pakistan Ordinance
21 of 1960 , for "Chief Court".)[High Court] in person or by
their advocates or pleaders.
The (Subs.
by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960 , for "Chief Court".)[High
Court] when it has heard and considered the case shall send a copy of its
decision, with the reasons therefor, under the seal of the Court, to the
Government by which the reference was made, and. subject to any appeal which
may be presented to, (Subs by P. O. No. 1 of 1961, for
"Her Majesty in Council" (w.e.f.23rd march, 1956).)[Supreme
Court] the case shall be disposed of conformably to such decision.
If the (Subs.
by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960, for "Chief Court''.)[High Court]
considers that any such statement is imperfectly framed, the (Subs. by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960, for "Chief
Court''.)[High Court] may return it for amendment.
The costs (if any) consequent on
any such reference shall be dealt with as the (Subs. by
Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960, for "Chief Court''.)[High Court] in
each case directs.

Power of Civil Judge to refer questions of jurisdiction to High Court

Act No

13. Power of Civil Judge to
refer questions of jurisdiction
to High Court.----If in any suit instituted, or in any appeal presented, in
a Civil Court, the Judge doubts whether he is precluded by this Act prom taking
cognizance of the suit or appeal, he may refer the matter to the (Subs. by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960, for "Chief
Court''.)[High Court].
The (Subs.
by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960, for "Chief Court''.)[High Court]
may order the Judge making , the reference either to proceed with the case or
to return the plaint.
The order of, the (Subs. by Pakistan Ordinance 21 of 1960, for "Chief
Court''.)[High Court] on any such reference shall be subject to appeal
to (Subs. by P.O. No. 1 of 1961, "Her Majesty in
Council" (w.e.f 23rd march, 1956).)[Supreme Court] and, save as
aforesaid, shall be final.

reference under section 12 or section 13 shall be heard by a Bench consisting

[16. Privileges of the
Government in suits defended by it.---( Subs. by
the Sind Revenue Jurisdiction (Amendment) Act, 1929 (Sind 21 of 1929). s.2, for
the original s. 16.)Whenever any suit is brought in any Court of
a Subordi nate Judge of the first class (The original
words "against Government" were first subs. by the A. O., 1937 and
then amended by G. G. O. 4 of 1949, Sch., and A. O., 1961, Art. 2, (w.ef. 23rd
March, 1956), to read as above.)[against the Government] or against any
Revenue-officer, (The original words "against
Government undertakes" were first subs. by the A. O. 1937, and then
amended by G. G. O. 4 of 1949, Sch., and A. O.,1961, Art. 2, (w.e.f. 23rd
March, 1956) to read as above.)[and the Government undertakes] the
defence there of, it shall be lawful] (Subs. by the A.
O.,1937, for "for the Government".)[for the Provincial Government],
by certificate signed by a Secretary thereto, to require that the trial of any
such suit shall have, precedence over the trial of any other suit or other
civil proceeding then pending in the Court of the first clays Subordi nate
Judge, or, if the suit is transferred, in the Court of the District Judge; and
the Court shall give effect to every such requirement.
The privilege conferred (Subs. by the A.O., 1937, for "on Government".)[on
the Provincial Government] by this section, shall mutatis mutandis, apply to
any appeal or special appeal against any decree in any such suit as is
described in this section.
